notes.chunk_at_written: … He had no children and no heirs; four biographies were commissioned by his own company and none was allowed out; the one he authorized he edited himself, and it ends in ascending triumph because it was published two years before he shot himself. He had also, across forty years of correspondence, let Thomas Edison be the famous one, knowing exactly what Edison could not see about his own inventions and keeping that judgment private. Now the company is gone as well, and what survives is a slide in a business school deck about an incumbent too stupid to see digital coming, which is not what happened. This book is the first honest accounting of him, and it can only be written now, because the image has finally left matter altogether. No lens, no light, no referent. …

before.text: **The company ran for another eighty years on his instructions, and this is the part that has been erased.** Tennessee Eastman operated the uranium plant at Oak Ridge for the Manhattan Project. Kodak built the cameras that flew over the Soviet Union and made the film that came back to earth in canisters snatched out of the sky by aircraft trailing hooks. In 1966 a Kodak system developed film while in orbit around the moon and radioed home the first photograph of the Earth. For most of a century it was among the most trusted names on the planet, and it is now a slide in a deck about incumbents who fail to adapt.
before.passage: **The company ran for another eighty years on his instructions, and this is the part that has been erased.** Tennessee Eastman operated the Y-12 plant at Oak Ridge from 1943 to 1947 and enriched the uranium for. Kodak made the film for America's first spy satellites, whose capsules came back out of orbit to be caught in midair by aircraft trailing hooks, and built the cameras for the programs that followed. August 1966 a Kodak system orbiting the moon developed its own film on board, scanned the negatives, and radioed home the first photograph of the Earth. At its peak Kodak held ninety percent of the American film market and was the fourth most valuable brand on the planet.
